# 1. Background

The goal was to predict the response to BSS using ROC analysis. We wanted to plot the predictive bacteria for responder and non-responders that were identified in day 0 data. The graphs are to show differences between responders and non-responders at day 0 as well as day 2 with pvalues. Then also plot the difference between day 0 and day 2 for responders and non- responders with pvalues. 


```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(stringr)
library(phyloseq)
library(metagMisc)
library(vegan)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggpubr)
library(rstatix)
library(knitr)

library(ggrepel)

library(kableExtra)
library(htmltools)
library(tidyverse)
library(pROC)
```

# 2. ROC analysis: class

ROC code provided by Ian LaCroix and adapted to suit microbiome data. 

## Data pre-processing 

```{r}

## The input data is formatted such that the first column has rows sequentially numbered, followed by columns containing the taxonomic ranks for/from phyloseq objects. 
## For example: 1;	OTU: Bacteroides_sp; kingdom: Bacteria; phylum: Bacteroidota; class:	Bacteroidia; order:	Bacteroidales; family: Bacteroidaceae; genus:	Bacteroides; species:	NA
## the remaining columns are sampleIDs which contain the normalized abundance of each genera 

data<-read.csv("Genus_counts_normalized.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE)
data[, c("order","family","genus","species","OTU","ATCCMSA2002control_P1",
         "ATCCMSA2002control_P2","NegativeControl","NegativeControl_P2","OTU.1")] <- NULL 
df_summed <- data %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE))

data<-as.data.frame(df_summed)

rownames(data)<-data$class
data[,c("class")]<-NULL


data<-as.data.frame(t(data))
data$Sample<-row.names(data)

## The first column in the metadata contains rows of sample IDs that correspond to the samples in the input data. Each subsequent column is a different piece of metadata.

metadata<-read.csv("BSS_metadata update10FEB2025.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE)


dat_merged <- merge.data.frame(metadata, data, by="Sample", all.x=FALSE, all.y=TRUE)

```


```{r results='hide'}

#### Data Pre Processing ####

clin_names <- dat_merged %>% 
  select(c(2:21)) %>% 
  names()


  
met_names <- dat_merged %>% 
  select(-c(1:21)) %>% 
  names()

dat_roc <- dat_merged %>% 
  filter(Timepoint == "Day 0") %>% 
  filter(Day2_obs != "N/A") %>% 
  select(Day2_obs, any_of(met_names))
```


<br><br>

--------


## ROC Analysis

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='hide'}

#### ROC Analysis ####
# initialize empty vectors
auc.vec <- c()
ci.low.vec <- c()
ci.upp.vec <- c()

# this loop calculates AUC (with 95% CI) for each analyte in predicting responder status
for(i in 1:length(met_names)){
  f <- as.formula(paste0("Day2_obs ~", met_names[i]))
  roc <- roc(f, data = dat_roc)
  auc <- auc(roc)
  auc.vec[i] <- auc
  ci <- as.data.frame(ci(roc))
  ci.low.vec[i] <- ci[1,]
  ci.upp.vec[i] <- ci[3,]
}




# create data frame of results
roc_results <- data.frame(met_names, 
                          "AUC" = auc.vec, 
                          "CI_0.95_lower" = ci.low.vec, 
                          "CI_0.95_upper" = ci.upp.vec) %>% 
  #filter(AUC > 0.70) %>% 
  arrange(desc(AUC))

results<- roc_results %>% filter(AUC > 0.7)
names(results)[1]<-"genus"

```

<br><br>

### T.tests on abundances

```{r}

t_results = {}



for (i in results$genus) {
  test_result <- t.test(dat_roc[[i]]~Day2_obs, data=dat_roc)
  t_results[[i]] <- list(
    t_stat = round(test_result$statistic, digits=4),
    p_value = round(test_result$p.value, digits=4)
  )
}

x<-data.frame(do.call(rbind, t_results))
x$t_stat<-as.numeric(x$t_stat)
x$p_value<-as.numeric(x$p_value)

x$genus<-rownames(x)

results_combo<-merge.data.frame(x, results, by ="genus", all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE)
results_combo <- results_combo[order(results_combo$p_value, decreasing=FALSE),]
results_combo<- results_combo %>% filter(p_value < 0.05)


results_combo %>% kable(caption="<strong>Table X. T.test results on abundances between responders and non-responders.<strong>", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:80%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Abundance stats" = 2, "ROC result" = 3))%>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 


library(downloadthis)
results_combo %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "ttest_abundance_results",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )
```


<br><br>

### Fold changes 

```{r}

#### Statistics ####

# calculate fold change (Responder/Non-Responder)
stat_results <- dat_roc %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -Day2_obs, names_to = "met_names", values_to = "Value") %>%
  group_by(met_names) %>%
  mutate(Fold_change = mean(Value[Day2_obs == "Responder"])/mean(Value[Day2_obs == "Non-responder"]), 
         lg2FC = log2(Fold_change), 
         p_val = t.test(Value ~ Day2_obs)$p.val,
         neg_log_p_val = -log10(p_val)
         #fdr_adj_p_val = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
         #neg_log_fdr_adj_p_val = -log10(fdr_adj_p_val)
         ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-Value, -Day2_obs) %>% 
  distinct(met_names, .keep_all = TRUE)


# focus on necessary stat columns
stat_results_trim <- stat_results %>% 
  select(met_names, lg2FC, neg_log_p_val) 

names(stat_results_trim)[1]<-"genus"

# Merge and Save Results
out_day_0 <- inner_join(stat_results_trim, results, by = "genus") %>%
  mutate(Time_point = "Day 0") %>%
  #select(-Clean_names) %>% 
  arrange(desc(AUC))

## write.csv(out_day_0, file = paste(Sys.Date(), "Responders_Day_0_ROC_Results_genus.csv", sep = "_"), row.names = FALSE)

out_day_0 <- out_day_0[order(out_day_0$neg_log_p_val, decreasing=TRUE),]
out_day_0 <- out_day_0 %>% filter(neg_log_p_val > 1.301)

out_day_0[,"Time_point"]<-NULL
out_day_0 %>% kable(caption="<strong>Table X. Results from ROC analysis and statistics. P values were converted to negative log pvalues, where anything >1.3 represents a pvalue of less than 0.05.<strong>", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:80%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Fold change stats" = 2, "ROC result" = 3))%>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 


library(downloadthis)
out_day_0 %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "ttest_fold_change_results",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

```

### ROC Curve

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

#### ROC Curve Plotting ####
top_features <- results_combo %>% 
  slice(1:47) %>% 
  pull(genus)


hit_list <- list()

for(i in 1:length(top_features)){
  f <- as.formula(paste0("Day2_obs ~", top_features[i]))
  roc_obj <- roc(f, data = dat_roc)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    FPR = rev(1 - roc_obj$specificities),
    TPR = rev(roc_obj$sensitivities),
    Model = as.character(top_features[i]),
    AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  )
  
  hit_list[[i]] <- df
}

# create data frame of results
roc_result <- bind_rows(hit_list)

roc_result %>% kable(caption="<strong>Table X. Results from ROC analysis for plotting.<strong>", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:80%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 


library(downloadthis)
roc_result %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "ROC_results_all_for_plotting",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

#write.csv(roc_result, "ROC_results_all_for_plotting.csv")

```

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results='hide'}

#### ROC Curve Plotting ####
top_features <-  out_day_0$genus


hit_list <- list()

for(i in 1:length(top_features)){
  f <- as.formula(paste0("Day2_obs ~", top_features[i]))
  roc_obj <- roc(f, data = dat_roc)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    FPR = rev(1 - roc_obj$specificities),
    TPR = rev(roc_obj$sensitivities),
    Model = as.character(top_features[i]),
    AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  )
  
  hit_list[[i]] <- df
}

# create data frame of results
roc_result <- bind_rows(hit_list)

```

```{r fig.cap="**Figure X. ROC curve showing top classes that predict a response.**", warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# Plot ROC Curves
roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_result, aes(x = FPR, y = TPR, color = Model, group = Model)) +
  geom_line(size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Day 0 ROC Curves", x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate") +
  theme_minimal()+ scale_colour_brewer(type="qual", palette="Paired")+scale_fill_brewer(type="qual", palette="Paired")
# View the plot
plot(roc_plot)

roc_plot %>% download_this(
    output_name = "ROC_curve",
    output_extension = ".pdf",
    button_label = "Download figure as .pdf",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa-solid fa-image",
    ggsave_args = list(height=4, width=5, limitsize=FALSE)
    
  )

ggexport(roc_plot, filename="ROC_plot_class.pdf", width=6, height=4)

```

# 3. Plotting predictive classes

## Import data

Create phyloseq object. 

```{r}
list<-data.frame(top_features)

data<-read.csv("Genus_counts_normalized.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE)
data[, c("order","family","genus","species","OTU","ATCCMSA2002control_P1",
         "ATCCMSA2002control_P2","NegativeControl","NegativeControl_P2","OTU.1")] <- NULL 
df_summed <- data %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE))

data<-as.data.frame(df_summed)

rownames(data)<-data$class

list$class<-list$top_features

predictors<-merge.data.frame(data, list, by="class", all.x=FALSE, all.y=FALSE)

rownames(predictors)<-predictors$class
predictors[,"class"]<-NULL
df<-predictors[,1:124]

df<-as.data.frame(t(df))
df$Sample<-rownames(df)

data<-merge.data.frame(df, metadata, by="Sample", all.x=TRUE, all.y=FALSE)

genes<-data[,c(2:6)]
gene_names<-colnames(genes)

```

## Plot customizations

Identify max values for each taxa plot and y.position of brackets for each comparison. 


```{r}

## prep data for day0 comparison between responder and non-responder

stat_results<-stat_results %>% filter(neg_log_p_val > 1.3)

max_values <- list()
# Loop through each gene name
for (gene in gene_names) { 
  max_values[[gene]]<- max(times[[gene]], na.rm = TRUE)  # Calculate max and handle NAs if any
}

max_values_df <- data.frame(
  gene = names(max_values),
  max_value = unlist(max_values)
)

max_values_df$max_values_add<-max_values_df$max_value
max_values_df$y.position<-log(max_values_df$max_values_add)*0.50
max_values_df$ymax<-(max_values_df$max_value*10) + max_values_df$max_value

max_values_df$group<-max_values_df$gene  
all_DAA_max.x<-merge.data.frame(max_values_df, stat_results, by="group", all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE)
all_DAA_max.x$y.position<-as.numeric(all_DAA_max.x$y.position)
all_DAA_max.x$pval<-round(all_DAA_max.x$pval, digits=3)
all_DAA_max.x$bracket1<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.2
all_DAA_max.x$bracket2<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.4
all_DAA_max.x$bracket3<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.6
all_DAA_max.x$bracket4<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.9

all_DAA_max.x$species<-all_DAA_max.x$group
all_DAA_max.x<-na.omit(all_DAA_max.x)

```





```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Prep data for loop. 
library(dplyr)

# split data for main graph ymax. 


# split data for each comparison and placement of bracket. Had to do this separately 
# so I could order the positions for each plot specifically. 

split_data.x<-split(all_DAA_max.x, f = all_DAA_max.x$group)


## list of plots for loop below. 
plots2<-list()


## reorder the x axis 

times$combined<- factor(times$combined,
    levels = c('Responder Day 0','Non-responder Day 0'), ordered = TRUE)

# remove NA values for day 0 (subject that has no responder status because no day 2 data)
times<-times[-c(6),]



```

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE }

# Loop to make graphs for each taxa. 

for (i in gene_names) {
  
plot<-ggplot(times, aes_string(x="combined", y=i))  + geom_violin() + geom_point(position =  position_jitter(width = 0.2, height=0, seed=1), size=3, aes(color=combined, group=Day2_obs)) + theme_bw() + ylab(i) + xlab(NULL) +theme(plot.margin = margin(c(20,10,20,10), 'cm'), axis.title.x=element_blank(), axis.text.x=element_text(size=20, angle=45, hjust=1), axis.text.y=element_text(size=20),  axis.title.y=element_text(size=15), plot.title = element_text(size=20), legend.position="none", legend.title=element_text(size=24), legend.text=element_text(size=20)) + ggtitle(i)+labs(x=NULL, y="Abundance") +stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="crossbar", size=0.5, color="black")  + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(NA, split_data.x[[i]]$ymax), trans="log10")+scale_colour_manual(values = c("#006d2c","#6baed6"))+scale_x_discrete(labels=c("High Resp. Day 0", "Low Resp. Day 0"))
  

## each stat_pvalue_manual has a separate list of data to pull from so that the placement of brackets is the same for each plots

plots2[[i]] <- plot2
    
}
```

```{r}
  arrange(desc(AUC))

## write.csv(out_day_0, file = paste(Sys.Date(), "Responders_Day_0_ROC_Results_genus.csv", sep = "_"), row.names = FALSE)

out_day_0 <- out_day_0[order(out_day_0$neg_log_p_val, decreasing=TRUE),]
out_day_0 <- out_day_0 %>% filter(neg_log_p_val > 1.301)

out_day_0[,"Time_point"]<-NULL
out_day_0 %>% kable(caption="<strong>Table X. Results from ROC analysis and statistics. P values were converted to negative log pvalues, where anything >1.3 represents a pvalue of less than 0.05.<strong>", format="html", full_width = FALSE, table.attr= "style='width:80%;'") %>% kable_styling(position="left", bootstrap_options = c("striped")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Fold change stats" = 2, "ROC result" = 3))%>% 
  scroll_box(width = "750px", height="650px", fixed_thead=T) 


library(downloadthis)
out_day_0 %>%
  download_this(
    output_name = "ttest_fold_change_results",
    output_extension = ".xlsx",
    button_label = "Download results in excel",
    button_type = "default",
    has_icon = TRUE,
    icon = "fa fa-save"
  )

```

<br><br>

> **Notes:** The genera whose abundances from day 0 to day 2 were significant with a pvalue of <0.05 with an AUC of 0.7 of greater were consider predictors. Other ideas for more conservative cuts could be the fold change (for example, anything >1 or <1 or increasing the AUC cutoff.)

<br><br>

Calculating log2fold changes for taxa that have zeros in high responders. 

```{r}


halo<-data.frame(dat_roc$Day2_obs, dat_roc$Halosegnis)
glac<-data.frame(dat_roc$Day2_obs, dat_roc$Glaciihabitans)
halo$pseudo<-halo$dat_roc.Halosegnis+1

halo_log<-halo %>% mutate(Fold_change = mean(pseudo[dat_roc.Day2_obs == "Responder"])/mean(pseudo[dat_roc.Day2_obs == "Non-responder"]), 
         lg2FC = log2(Fold_change)) 

glac$pseudo<-glac$dat_roc.Glaciihabitans+1


glac_log<-glac %>% mutate(Fold_change = mean(pseudo[dat_roc.Day2_obs == "Responder"])/mean(pseudo[dat_roc.Day2_obs == "Non-responder"]), 
         lg2FC = log2(Fold_change)) 

```

# 5.Plotting predictive genera

## Import data

Create phyloseq object. 

```{r}
list<-read.csv("Top_predictors_ROC_all.csv")


genus<-read.csv("Genus_counts_normalized.csv", row.names=1, header=TRUE)


genus[, c("kingdom","phylum","class","order","family","species","OTU","OTU.1")] <- NULL

genus_df<-genus

list$genus<-list$met_names
predictors<-merge.data.frame(genus_df, list, by="genus", all.x=FALSE, all.y=FALSE)

rownames(predictors)<-predictors$genus
predictors[,"genus"]<-NULL
df<-predictors[,1:124]

df<-as.data.frame(t(df))
df$Sample<-rownames(df)

data<-merge.data.frame(df, metadata, by="Sample", all.x=TRUE, all.y=FALSE)

genes<-data[,c(2:48)]
gene_names<-colnames(genes)

gene_names

```

## Plot customizations

Identify max values for each taxa plot and y.position of brackets for each comparison. 


```{r}

## prep data for day0 comparison between responder and non-responder

stat_results<-stat_results %>% filter(neg_log_p_val > 1.3)

max_values <- list()
# Loop through each gene name
for (gene in gene_names) { 
  max_values[[gene]]<- max(times[[gene]], na.rm = TRUE)  # Calculate max and handle NAs if any
}

max_values_df <- data.frame(
  gene = names(max_values),
  max_value = unlist(max_values)
)

max_values_df$max_values_add<-max_values_df$max_value
max_values_df$y.position<-log(max_values_df$max_values_add)*0.50
max_values_df$ymax<-(max_values_df$max_value*10) + max_values_df$max_value

max_values_df$group<-max_values_df$gene  
all_DAA_max.x<-merge.data.frame(max_values_df, stat_results, by="group", all.x=TRUE, all.y=TRUE)
all_DAA_max.x$y.position<-as.numeric(all_DAA_max.x$y.position)
all_DAA_max.x$pval<-round(all_DAA_max.x$pval, digits=3)
all_DAA_max.x$bracket1<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.2
all_DAA_max.x$bracket2<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.4
all_DAA_max.x$bracket3<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.6
all_DAA_max.x$bracket4<-all_DAA_max.x$y.position*0.9

all_DAA_max.x$species<-all_DAA_max.x$group
all_DAA_max.x<-na.omit(all_DAA_max.x)

```





```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Prep data for loop. 
library(dplyr)

# split data for main graph ymax. 


# split data for each comparison and placement of bracket. Had to do this separately 
# so I could order the positions for each plot specifically. 

split_data.x<-split(all_DAA_max.x, f = all_DAA_max.x$group)


## list of plots for loop below. 
plots2<-list()


## reorder the x axis 

times$combined<- factor(times$combined,
    levels = c('Responder Day 0','Non-responder Day 0'), ordered = TRUE)

# remove NA values for day 0 (subject that has no responder status because no day 2 data)
times<-times[-c(6),]
```

### Separate

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE }

# Loop to make graphs for each taxa. 

for (i in gene_names) {
  
plot<-ggplot(times, aes_string(x="combined", y=i))  + geom_violin() + geom_point(position =  position_jitter(width = 0.2, height=0, seed=1), size=3, aes(color=combined, group=Day2_obs)) + theme_bw() + ylab(i) + xlab(NULL) +theme(plot.margin = margin(c(20,10,20,10), 'cm'), axis.title.x=element_blank(), axis.text.x=element_text(size=20, angle=45, hjust=1), axis.text.y=element_text(size=20),  axis.title.y=element_text(size=15), plot.title = element_text(size=20), legend.position="none", legend.title=element_text(size=24), legend.text=element_text(size=20)) + ggtitle(i)+labs(x=NULL, y="Abundance") +stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="crossbar", size=0.5, color="black")  + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(NA, split_data.x[[i]]$ymax), trans="log10")+scale_colour_manual(values = c("#006d2c","#6baed6"))+scale_x_discrete(labels=c("High Resp. Day 0", "Low Resp. Day 0"))
  

## each stat_pvalue_manual has a separate list of data to pull from so that the placement of brackets is the same for each plots


plot2<-plot +stat_pvalue_manual(split_data.x[[i]][1,], label = "p={pval}", xmin = "group1", xmax="group2", size=4.5)

plots2[[i]] <- plot2
    
}




```
